title: The Stoic trick for a calmer mind
summary: Epictetus taught that some things are up to us — our judgments and actions — and most things are not. Putting your energy only into the first pile is the core of Stoic calm.
evidenceNote: This is a philosophical idea, not a scientific finding. Modern cognitive therapies draw on similar thinking, but the Stoic framework itself is a way of seeing, not a proven treatment.

scenes.text: "Some things are in our control and others not." — Epictetus
Epictetus was born into slavery around 50 CE and became one of the most influential Stoic teachers.
He sorted life into two piles.
A delayed train isn't up to you. How you spend the wait is.
Does that mean you stop caring about results?
scenes.answer: No. The Stoics compared it to an archer: aim as well as you can, then accept where the arrow lands.

scenes.text: Spend your energy where it actually works.
